criteria.text: User Action: Opens the “Chores” tab. Expected System Behavior: The Chore List opens with the household name in the header and the “All” filter selected.

The progress card shows "[X] of [Y] chores done" with a progress bar and a status label (Status: On track/ Complete!/ {num} Late), or "No Chores Yet" when no chores are due. The progress bar tracks tasks that are due this week. If the chore is a monthly chore, then it is counted in the final week of the month.
criteria.note: Corrected to Figma's labels (team decision). Jira still says "On track/ Complete/ {num} late/ N/A". There are no monthly (recurring) chores yet (TECH_SPEC §11), so that sentence has nothing to test.

criteria.text: Each open chore card shows the chore name, the assigned housemate ("You" if it is the user), and the due date (e.g., "due today," "due tomorrow," "due Fri, Oct 9"), plus a checkbox if the chore is assigned to the user.
criteria.note: Corrected (team decision: only the assignee can tick a chore). Jira still says every open card shows a checkbox.

criteria.text: A chore past its due date is highlighted and shows an “Overdue” chip.
An overdue chore that has been completed has a “Late” chip.
User Action: Clicks “Mine.” Expected System Behavior: Only chores assigned to the user are shown.
User Action: Clicks “All.” Expected System Behavior: All household chores are shown.
Completed chores appear under “Done ([count])” below the open chores, with the name struck through and a “Done” chip.
User Action: Clicks “Done ([count]).” Expected System Behavior: The section expands or collapses.
User Action: Clicks “Add chore.” Expected System Behavior: The “Add chore” screen opens.

User Action: Clicks arrow on right-side of chore card. Expected System Behavior: Chore details pane slides open underneath chore card containing chore information not already on chore card. Includes “Last done” : date, “by” : user, and an “Edit” button visible to users with edit permissions.
criteria.note: The arrow is a chevron to the right of the chip (Figma “Schedule”, 837:1483); the chore's name opens it too. The Edit button is Figma's pencil, shown to the household owner and the chore's creator until SCRUM-62 makes it the household manager, and it opens Edit chore. README Conflicts rows 28–31.

criteria.text: Error Condition: Chores fail to load. Message: "Couldn't load chores." with a "Try again" button.
criteria.note: Corrected to the app's wording (team decision). Jira still says "We couldn't load your chores. Please try again."
